newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends weaker, benchmark shifts to Dec.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends weaker, benchmark shifts to Dec.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen futures contract ended the day session easier on Tuesday in sympathy with weak yen bond futures, traders said.
A TIFFE spokesman said the September stepped down from the benchmark status and the December took the key bond position.
Small lot selling in the December was in response to traders' wariness towards holding long positions as the market had already been close to the record high levels.
The majority of the Euroyen futures market believes that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) is unlikely to tighten credit in the first half of this calender year.
But in the futures options market, some expect a more aggressive credit easing.
Traders said 4,300 put option contracts for June 1997 were sold at 99.25, pushing it down to 99.22.
The move reflected a view that the BOJ may not just maintain its ultra-easy credit policy until June, but may even cut interest rates further by then, traders said.
In the Eurodollar deposit market, the "Japan premium", the extra cost of funding for Japanese banks, widened on Tuesday.

Traders said the premium rose on market talk on Monday about financial problems at Japanese banks, the recent weakness in share prices and the lowering in credit rating outlook for four Japanese banks by Moody's Investors Service on Monday.

Major Japanese banks were paying a premium of about 19 basis points over the prevailing three-month Eurodollar deposit rate of 5.53125 percent, traders said. This compared with a premium of about six basis points in the second week of January.
The key three month certificate of deposit was traded at 0.53 percent, unchanged from Monday.
The overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.49 percent, also unchanged from Monday.
The BOJ offset a projected fund shortfall of 720 billion yen by injecting 700 billion yen into the market in its regular 0020 GMT operation.
